output.headline: Amends dual-enrollment agreement with Peralta Community College District for online learning
output.summary: This changes the existing College and Career Access Pathways Act (CCAP) agreement under which Peralta Community College District teaches college pathway courses to Oakland high school students. The amendment allows online and distance learning because of the COVID-19 pandemic, names the district's representative, and covers increases in state funding for dual enrollment and special populations. All other terms stay the same.

output.headline: Approves 3-year contract with the school administrators' union, with 5% raises
output.summary: This adopts a tentative agreement with United Administrators of Oakland Schools (UAOS), the union for certificated and classified administrators, covering July 1, 2019 through June 30, 2022. It includes a 5% ongoing raise starting July 1, 2020 for employees who are not retiring, a 5% raise effective January 1, 2020 for those who retire on or before June 30, 2020, and bonuses described in the agreement. The text gives no dollar totals.

output.headline: Lets the Chief Business Officer sign vendor contracts up to $50,000 a year
output.summary: This updates Board Policy 3312 so the Chief Business Officer can enter into contracts with a single vendor without a separate board vote, up to $50,000 in total in a fiscal year. It changes who has signing authority; it does not spend money by itself.

output.headline: Partners with Roses in Concrete charter school to bring it into Howard Elementary
output.summary: This memorandum of understanding (MOU) sets up a partnership in which Roses in Concrete, a charter school, will operate at Howard Elementary School, a District school. It starts with a "Design Year" in School Year 2020-21. The text does not state a dollar amount.
